Sunlight appears white but is actually composed of all the colors of the visible spectrum, each with a different wavelength. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, the shorter blue wavelengths scatter much more strongly off nitrogen and oxygen molecules than the longer red wavelengths—a process called Rayleigh scattering. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every direction in the sky, making it appear blue to us.
